What it means: Keep working files in one place the team can reach, with access that survives staff turnover.
Example question: Where should our project team keep interview files while the study runs?

What it means: Work on the same files, data or analysis with people at another institution.
Example question: Can a researcher at USM edit our shared folder?

What it means: Store, analyse or share personal or confidential data under proper control.
Example question: Where may we keep student records for a study?

What it means: Build and run questionnaires, online or on paper-replacement devices.
Example question: What should we use for a survey of 400 teachers?

What it means: Collect data in the field without a reliable internet connection.
Example question: Can enumerators collect household data offline and sync later?

What it means: Make a dataset openly findable and downloadable, with documentation and a licence.
Example question: Where do we put the data behind a published article?

What it means: Give outputs a persistent, citable identifier (DOI).
Example question: How do we get DOIs for our reports and datasets?

What it means: Host an institution's own branded repository.
Example question: Should we set up our own repository or use an existing one?

What it means: Keep outputs preserved and accessible for decades, beyond any one website or staff member.
Example question: How do we make sure this survey is still available in 2040?

What it means: Make theses, reports and working-paper series openly available.
Example question: Where do our bachelor and master theses go?

What it means: Persistent identifiers for researchers (ORCID) and institutions (ROR).
Example question: How do we make sure outputs are credited to our institution?

What it means: Descriptive and inferential statistics on quantitative data.
Example question: What can replace our SPSS licence for everyday analysis?

What it means: Regression, panel and time-series models, forecasting.
Example question: What can students use to learn econometrics without an EViews licence?

What it means: Teach statistics, coding or data skills to students and staff.
Example question: What should we use in the first-year statistics course?

What it means: Analysis that can be rerun and checked from a script or saved workflow.
Example question: How do we make sure next year's report can be rebuilt from the data?

What it means: Code interviews, focus groups, field notes and documents.
Example question: What can our master students use to code interviews?

What it means: Turn recorded interviews into text.
Example question: How can we transcribe interviews without uploading them to a cloud service?

What it means: Combine qualitative and quantitative data in one project.
Example question: How do we link interview codes to survey answers?

What it means: Prediction, classification, clustering and text mining.
Example question: Where can staff start with machine learning?

What it means: Charts and dashboards to communicate results.
Example question: How do we publish our key figures as a dashboard?

What it means: Track changes to code, lessons and documents over time.
Example question: How do we keep track of versions of our analysis scripts?

What it means: Share course materials openly and citably so others can reuse them.
Example question: How can another island reuse our course?

What it means: Write a data management plan for a grant or project.
Example question: The funder asks for a data management plan. Where do we start?

What it means: Use AI assistants for work without putting personal or confidential data where it should not go.
Example question: Can a lecturer paste student essays into a chatbot to help with grading?

What it means: Decide how students and teachers may use AI, and how AI use is checked.
Example question: What should our AI policy say about detectors and grading?
